text.p: -- Hambrecht & Quist cut its rating on Sun Microsystems Inc to buy from strong buy, but raised its earnings estimates after Sun reported March quarter earnings late on Tuesday.
-- It raised its fiscal 1997 earnings estimate to $1.88/shr from $1.83 and fiscal 1998 to $2.30 from $2.05.

-- In a statement, the investment research firm said sales and order growth at the high-end computer company were less than expected due to a product transition from desktop workstations to servers, storage systems and software. The servers, storage systems and software business in the future, however, will generate higher growth rates and gross margins.
-- "We believe the transition will create a period of slower revenue growth accompanied by faster earnings growth and strong cash flow," Hambrecht said.
-- It cut the stock rating on a near-term basis "to reflect the transition risk."
